Entry into the home and subsequent discovery of the firearm

outline.description: Explains the legal framework governing consent searches of a dwelling, including the statutory exception, the voluntariness standard, and the scope analysis, with citations to controlling Supreme Court and Seventh Circuit precedent.
subtopics: Consent as an exception to the warrant requirement (Banks, Schneckloth v. Bustamonte)
Third‑party consent and the Matlock/Cellitti line
Freely and voluntarily standard (Bumper v. North Carolina)
Totality‑of‑circumstances factors (Figueroa‑Espana, Santiago)
Objective‑reasonableness test for scope of consent (Jimeno)
Standard of review on appeal (clear error/abuse of discretion)

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Analysis of Voluntariness of Lisa Coleman’s Consent
outline.description: Applies the consent doctrine to the facts, evaluating whether Lisa’s statements and actions constitute a free and voluntary relinquishment of her Fourth Amendment rights.
subtopics: Initial refusal and subsequent acquiescence – significance of the two requests
Officer Kizer’s tone, demeanor, and lack of coercion
Absence of custody, length of interaction, and opportunity to refuse

Objective‑reasonableness inquiry – what a reasonable person would infer

Court’s finding of no overreach and its implications
